title: Protestant imperfecta means incomplete in degree
source_text: XXV. Huc vero non alio spectant quae Theologi Protestantes docent de imperfec-tione justitiae illius quae per Christi gratiam fidelibus inhaeret. Etenim, quum per-tendunt illam inchoatam duntaxat & imperfectam esse, non perfectam atque absolutam; id non aliud significatum volunt, quam justitiam istam in terris nunquam attingere ipsum perfectionis & excellentiae gradum, quin plurimum ab eo abesse: ideoque per gradus varios quotidie augendam, & promovendam esse; donec tandem in vita fu-tura plene consummetur & perficiatur. Ac praeterea fideles quantumcunque in justitia & sanctitate profecerint, suos semper habere defectus, & multis lapsibus manere ob-noxios, donec corpus hoc mortale exuerint.
pass_a_gloss: But what Protestant theologians teach about the imperfection of that righteousness which by Christ's grace inheres in believers looks to no other point. For when they maintain that it is only begun and imperfect, not perfect and absolute, they mean nothing else than that that righteousness on earth never attains the very degree of perfection and excellence, but is far from it; and therefore must daily be increased and advanced by various degrees until at last in the life to come it is fully consummated and perfected. And besides, that believers, however far they have advanced in righteousness and holiness, always have their defects and remain liable to many falls until they put off this mortal body.
pass_b_english: When Protestants call inherent justice inchoate and imperfect, they mean it never reaches the highest degree on earth.
It must daily advance until consummated hereafter; the regenerate keep defects until death.

choices.why: Degree-language, not denial of true holiness.
